definitions.gloss: in name only; nominal; only in title
definitions.explanation: Describes something or someone that holds a title, name, or label but lacks the substance, authority, or quality that the name implies. Carries a critical or dismissive nuance.

examples.japanese: {名|な}ばかりの{管理職|かんりしょく}だ。
examples.english: He's a manager in name only.

examples.japanese: ここは{名|な}ばかりの{高級|こうきゅう}レストランで、{料理|りょうり}は{普通|ふつう}だった。
examples.english: This is a supposedly high-end restaurant in name only; the food was ordinary.

examples.japanese: {名|な}ばかりの{改革|かいかく}では{国民|こくみん}の{信頼|しんらい}は{得|え}られない。
examples.english: Reforms in name only will not win the trust of the people.

notes:
USAGE:
{名|な}ばかり modifies nouns with の: {名|な}ばかりの{社長|しゃちょう} (a president in name only). It is a critical expression implying that the reality does not match the label. The word is a compound of {名|な} (name) + ばかり (only/just).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {名|な}ばかりの{社長|しゃちょう} (president in name only)
- {名|な}ばかりの{専門家|せんもんか} (expert in name only)
- {名|な}ばかりの{自由|じゆう} (freedom in name only)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{形|かたち}だけの means 'only for show' or 'only in form' and is close in meaning. {有名無実|ゆうめいむじつ} is a four-character idiom meaning 'in name but not in reality.' {名|な}ばかり is the most commonly used in everyday speech.
